questions.prompt: Huygens' principle states that:
choices: Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets
Light always travels in straight lines
Waves cannot interfere
Wavefronts are always planar
questions.answer: Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets
questions.explanation: The new wavefront is the envelope of the secondary wavelets.

questions.prompt: When light enters glass from air, its frequency stays the same while its wavelength decreases.
questions.explanation: Frequency is set by the source; the speed drops, so λ = v/f decreases.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of constructing a new wavefront with Huygens' principle in order.
items: Choose points along the current wavefront
Draw secondary wavelets of radius vΔt from each point
Draw the common tangent to the wavelets
The tangent is the new wavefront
questions.explanation: The new wavefront is the envelope of the wavelets.

questions.prompt: Light of wavelength 500 nm passes through two slits 0.25 mm apart onto a screen 1.5 m away. What is the fringe spacing in mm?
Which statements about thin-film interference are true?
choices: A whole-number path difference in wavelengths gives constructive interference
A half-integer path difference gives destructive interference
Reflection from a lower-index medium causes a half-wave phase shift
Reflection from a higher-index medium causes a half-wave phase shift
answers: A whole-number path difference in wavelengths gives constructive interference
A half-integer path difference gives destructive interference
Reflection from a higher-index medium causes a half-wave phase shift
questions.explanation: A phase flip happens only on reflection off a higher-index medium.

questions.prompt: Match each pattern to its condition or formula.
questions.explanation: These are the standard conditions for each setup.

questions.prompt: Light of wavelength 400 nm strikes a metal with work function 2.0 eV. What is the maximum kinetic energy of the ejected electrons in eV, to one decimal place? Use hc = 1240 eV·nm.
Above threshold, increasing the intensity of light while keeping its frequency fixed will:
choices: Increase the number of photoelectrons per second
Increase the maximum kinetic energy of electrons
Decrease the stopping potential
Eliminate the threshold frequency
questions.answer: Increase the number of photoelectrons per second
questions.explanation: More photons per second eject more electrons, but each photon's energy hf is unchanged.

questions.prompt: What effect describes the increase in wavelength of X-rays scattered off electrons?
questions.explanation: The Compton effect shows photons carrying momentum p = h/λ.

questions.prompt: What is the de Broglie wavelength in nm of an electron (m = 9.11×10⁻³¹ kg) moving at 1.0×10⁶ m/s, to two decimal places? Use h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s.
The Heisenberg uncertainty principle arises because our instruments are not precise enough.
questions.explanation: It is a fundamental property of quantum systems, not a limit of measurement technology.

questions.prompt: Which statements describe the double-slit experiment with single electrons?
choices: Each electron lands at a localized spot
An interference pattern builds up over many electrons
The pattern disappears if which-slit is measured
Each electron splits into two electrons
answers: Each electron lands at a localized spot
An interference pattern builds up over many electrons
The pattern disappears if which-slit is measured
questions.explanation: Electrons are detected as whole particles but their distribution shows wave interference.

questions.prompt: What is the energy in eV, to two decimal places, of the photon emitted in the hydrogen n = 3 to n = 2 transition? Use E_n = −13.6/n² eV.
Which of these is a key failure of the Bohr model?
choices: It cannot explain atoms with more than one electron
It predicts no energy levels
It predicts the wrong hydrogen spectrum
It requires no quantization
questions.answer: It cannot explain atoms with more than one electron
questions.explanation: Bohr's model works for hydrogen-like atoms but fails for multielectron atoms.

questions.prompt: Match each hydrogen series to its final level.
questions.explanation: The series are named by the lower level of the transition.

questions.prompt: A particle in a box has ground-state energy E₁ = 2.0 eV. What is the energy of the n = 3 state in eV?
questions.explanation: Eₙ = n²E₁, so E₃ = 9(2.0) = 18 eV.

questions.prompt: The quantity |ψ|² gives the probability density of finding a particle.
questions.explanation: The Born interpretation says |ψ(x)|²dx is the probability of finding the particle in dx.

questions.prompt: Explain why a particle in a one-dimensional box has only quantized energies.
rubric: Says the wavefunction must be zero at the walls
Says only whole numbers of half-wavelengths fit in the box, L = nλ/2
Connects allowed wavelengths to allowed momentum or energy
questions.model: The wavefunction must vanish at the walls, so only standing waves with L = nλ/2 fit. Each allowed wavelength fixes the momentum p = h/λ and energy, giving Eₙ proportional to n², so only discrete values are possible.
questions.explanation: Boundary conditions force standing-wave solutions, which are discrete.

questions.prompt: How does the tunneling probability through a barrier change as the barrier gets wider?
choices: It decreases exponentially
It increases linearly
It stays constant
It increases exponentially
questions.explanation: The wavefunction decays exponentially inside the barrier, so wider barriers transmit much less.

questions.prompt: Which technologies rely on quantum mechanics?
choices: Lasers
Transistors
Scanning tunneling microscope
Mercury thermometer
questions.explanation: Lasers, semiconductor transistors, and STMs depend directly on quantum behavior; a mercury thermometer relies on classical thermal expansion.

questions.prompt: What is the process by which a particle crosses a classically forbidden barrier?
questions.explanation: Tunneling is a wave effect where the wavefunction penetrates the barrier.
